pass_a_gloss: And let us observe this also, that not in the speeches to the many are matters about martyrdom foretold by the Saviour, but in the speeches to the apostles. For with it said beforehand, these twelve Jesus sent off, having ordered them, into a road of nations do not depart, and the next things, there is brought on: watch out from the humans; for they will deliver you into sanhedrins, and in their gatherings they will whip you; and onto leaders and kings you will be led on my account, for a witness to them and to the nations. Whenever they deliver you, do not be anxious how or what you should talk; for it will be given you in that hour what you should talk; for you are not the ones talking, but the spirit of the father, which talks in you. A brother will deliver a brother into death, and a father a child, and children will stand up against begetters and make them die. And you will be ones hated by everyone through my name. The one having held out into an end, this one will be saved. Whenever they chase you in this city, run off into the other one, and if out of this one they chase, run off into the other. For amen I say to you, you will by no means complete the cities of Israel until the son of the human comes. And Luke writes up such things: whenever they carry you onto the gatherings and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious how you should make a defence speech or what you should say; for the holy spirit will instruct you in that same hour what is needful to say. And after other things: place it therefore in your hearts not to practise ahead to make a defence; for I will give you mouth and wisdom, which all the ones lying opposite you will not be able to stand against or speak against. You will be delivered also by begetters and brothers and kin and friends, and they will make die from among you, and you will be ones hated by everyone through my name. And a hair from your head will by no means perish; in your holding out acquire your souls. Such things Mark also says: whenever they lead you delivering you, do not be anxious ahead nor practise ahead what you should talk, but whatever may be given you in that hour, talk that; for you are not the ones talking but the holy spirit. A brother will deliver a brother into death and a father a child, and children will stand up against begetters and make them die. And you will be ones hated by everyone through my name; the one having held out into an end, this one will be saved. And these too, in Matthew, urging toward martyrdom, were said to no others than the twelve; whom it will be needful that we also hear, being about to be, in the hearing, brothers of the apostles who heard, and about to be counted along with apostles. The sayings hold thus: do not fear from the ones killing the body but not able to kill the soul; fear rather the one able to ruin both soul and body in gehenna. And next to these the lord teaches us that not without forethought does someone come onto the contest of martyrdom. For it is said: are not two little sparrows sold for an assarion? and one out of them will not fall onto the ground without the father in the heavens. Of you the hairs of the head are all counted. Do not then fear; you differ from many little sparrows. Everyone then who will confess in me in front of the humans, I also will confess in him in front of my father in the heavens; and whoever denies me in front of the humans, him I also will deny in front of my father in the heavens. Of equal force with these are the things in Luke: these things I say to you my friends: do not fear from the ones killing the body and after these things not having anything more to do. I will point out to you whom you should fear: fear the one who after the killing has authority to throw into gehenna. Yes, I say to you, fear this one. Are not five little sparrows sold for two assaria? and one out of them is not forgotten in the sight of God. But also the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not then fear; you differ from many little sparrows. And I say to you: everyone who confesses in me in front of the humans, the son of the human also will confess in him in front of the messengers of God; the one who denied me in the sight of the humans will be denied in the sight of the messengers of God. And in another spot: for whoever is shamed by me and my words, him the son of the human will be shamed by, whenever he comes in his glory and of the father and of the holy messengers. And near to this Mark too wrote up such a thing: for whoever is shamed by me and my words in the adulterous and sinning generation, the son of the human also will be shamed by him, whenever he comes in the glory of the father with the holy messengers. The ones doing away with us then kill a life of body; for such is the do not fear from the ones killing the body, said in the very words by Matthew and Luke. And after killing the body, even if they wish, they are not able to kill the soul; but neither do they have anything more to do. For how is it possible for a soul to be done away with, made alive by the confession itself? The one urging us toward martyrdom in Isaiah, and his boy, witnessing back to it, where it is written: become witnesses for me, and I a witness, says lord the God, and the boy whom I picked out. And keep this also, that not to slaves of Jesus but to his friends this order has been given: do not fear from the ones killing the body and after these things not having anything more to do. One must fear then the one able to ruin both soul and body in gehenna. For this one alone after the killing has authority to throw into gehenna. And he will throw in the ones who feared from the ones killing the body and who did not fear the one able to ruin both soul and body in gehenna and the one who after the killing has authority to throw into gehenna. If of anyone else the hairs of the head are counted, clearly also to those cut off at the head through Jesus. We will confess in the son of God, and in front of humans and not of gods, so that the one confessed may pay us back, having confessed us in front of the God and father of himself, and having confessed, he himself in the heavens, the one who confessed him on earth.
pass_b_english: Let us note this too: the Saviour's prophecies about martyrdom come not in his words to the crowds but in his words to the apostles. For after the passage “These twelve Jesus sent out, charging them, ‘Do not go off on the road of the Gentiles’” (Matthew 10:5), and what follows, there comes: “Beware of men; for they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you; and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles. When they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you are to speak, for what you are to speak will be given you in that hour; for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of the Father speaking in you. Brother will hand over brother to death, and father child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death. And you will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved. When they persecute you in this city, flee to the other; and if they persecute you out of that one, flee to another. For truly I tell you, you will not finish the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes” (Matthew 10:17-23).

Luke records words of the same kind: “When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say; for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you must say” (Luke 12:11-12). And after other things: “So settle it in your hearts not to rehearse your defence; for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which none of those who oppose you will be able to withstand or contradict. You will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death, and you will be hated by all because of my name. And not a hair of your head will perish. By your endurance gain your souls” (Luke 21:14-19).

Mark too says the like: “When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand or rehearse what you are to speak, but whatever is given you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit. Brother will hand over brother to death, and father child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death. And you will be hated by all because of my name; but the one who endures to the end will be saved” (Mark 13:11-13).

These words too in Matthew, which urge us on to martyrdom, were spoken to none other than the Twelve. We also shall need to hear them, since by hearing them we shall become brothers of the apostles who heard them and shall be counted among the apostles. The sayings run like this: “Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna” (Matthew 10:28). And next after these the Lord teaches us that no one comes to the contest of martyrdom without providence. For it is said: “Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall to the ground without the Father who is in heaven. As for you, the hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. Everyone, then, who confesses in me before men, I too will confess in him before my Father who is in heaven; but whoever denies me before men, I too will deny him before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:29-33).

Equivalent to these are the words in Luke: “I say these things to you, my friends: do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do. But I will show you whom to fear: fear him who, after killing, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him. Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten before God. Why, even the hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. And I tell you, everyone who confesses in me before men, the Son of Man too will confess in him before the angels of God; but the one who denies me before men will be denied before the angels of God” (Luke 12:4-9). And in another place: “For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels” (Luke 9:26). Mark too recorded something close to this: “For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in the adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man too will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of the Father with the holy angels” (Mark 8:38).

So those who put us to death kill a bodily life; for that is the force of “Do not be afraid of those who kill the body”, a saying given in the very same words by Matthew and by Luke. And after killing the body, even if they want to, they cannot kill the soul; indeed they do not have “anything more to do”. For how could a soul be destroyed that has been made alive by the confession itself? The one who urges us on to martyrdom in Isaiah, and his servant, bear witness to it in return, where it is written: “Become my witnesses, and I am a witness, says the Lord God, and the servant whom I have chosen” (Isaiah 43:10).

Note this too: this command was given not to Jesus' slaves but to his friends: “Do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do” (Luke 12:4). We must therefore fear “him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna”. For he alone, “after killing”, has “authority to cast into Gehenna”. And he will indeed cast into it those who were afraid of those who kill the body and were not afraid of “him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna” and of “him who after killing has authority to cast into Gehenna”. If the hairs of anyone's head are numbered, plainly those of the ones beheaded for Jesus' sake are numbered too. We will confess in the Son of God, before men and not before gods, so that the one we confessed may repay us, confessing us before his God and Father, and himself confessing in heaven the one who confessed him on earth.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 34); the old English was a digest. It began with Matthew 10:16 (not quoted by Origen), dropped Luke 12:11-12, Luke 12:4-9 and Luke 9:26, inserted Mark 13:9-10 and John 15:15, extended Isaiah 43:10 beyond Origen's quotation, and dropped Origen's comments on providence, on the soul made alive by confession, and on confessing in the Son.
